name: The Honest Salesman
blurb: A salesman who physically cannot lie has one day to sell a truly terrible toaster
title: The Honest Salesman: Funny Skit Script for 3 People
description: A 5-minute comedy skit script for 3: a salesman who cannot lie must sell a terrible smart toaster, and every pitch comes out true. Free to perform.
h1: The Honest Salesman: a 5-Minute Comedy Skit Script for 3 People
logline: Vince has one day to sell a single Smart Toaster Pro or lose his job. There is one problem: he physically cannot lie, so every sales pitch turns into the truth halfway through the sentence. His manager is getting desperate, and the customer seems to be enjoying it far too much.
setting: A small shop counter. Props: a table, a shoebox decorated as a toaster with stickers (a torch or phone light inside for the blinking light), a name badge, a wallet, a small card.

roles.name: Vince
roles.note: Adult, written as a man (rename freely for any gender). Kind, desperate to keep his job, cannot lie.

roles.name: Morgan
roles.note: Adult, any gender. The shop manager. Smiles all the time, panics inside.

roles.name: Kim
roles.note: Adult, written as a woman (any gender works). The customer. Calm, curious, secretly an inspector.

script.action: A table with a shoebox-sized "toaster" on it, covered in stickers and a blinking light. MORGAN, the shop manager, straightens VINCE's name badge.

script.say: Vince. This is your last chance. You have sold nothing in three weeks.
I know.
The Smart Toaster Pro. We have four hundred of them in the back. Sell one today or you're out.
Morgan, you know my problem. I can't lie. Not "I don't like lying." I physically cannot. My mouth won't do it.
Then don't lie. Just... choose happy words.

script.action: A bell rings. KIM enters, looking around.

script.say: Go. Happy words.

script.action: Morgan steps aside and pretends to tidy a shelf, watching. Vince approaches Kim with a huge smile.

script.say: Good morning! Looking for a toaster?
I am, actually. Mine broke.
Then you're in luck. This is the Smart Toaster Pro. It's the fastest toaster in the—

script.action: Vince's mouth twists. He fights it. He loses.

script.say: —the slowest toaster I have ever seen. It takes forty minutes. For one slice.
Forty minutes?
Forty-two if it's brown bread.

script.action: Morgan coughs loudly from the shelf. Vince tries again.

script.say: But! It's smart. It connects to your phone. You can control it from anywhere in the—
—anywhere in the kitchen. Only the kitchen. It loses the signal if you leave the room. And sometimes it posts a photo of your toast online without asking.
Why would it do that?
Nobody knows. We've asked it.
What Vince means is, it's a very social toaster. Tell her about the price, Vince. The amazing price.
It's an amazing price. Three hundred. That's about six normal toasters. Or one normal toaster and a very nice dinner.
That's a lot of money for slow toast.
It is. I wouldn't buy it.
Vince.
Sorry. I would buy it if someone held me upside down.
Tell her about the warranty.
Two years. But the shop's policy is to hope you lose the receipt. Morgan says that at every meeting.
Can I see it work?
Of course.

script.action: Vince presses the button. The light blinks. Nothing happens. They wait. Kim looks at Vince. Vince looks at the toaster.

script.say: This is the exciting part. Where nothing happens. For forty minutes.
That beep means it's thinking about starting.
Let me help. Madam, the Smart Toaster Pro is the best purchase you will ever make. Everyone who buys it is delighted. It changed my life.
Really?
Absolutely. Vince, tell her. Is this the best purchase of her life?

script.action: Vince opens his mouth. Closes it. Opens it. Everyone waits.

script.say: Honestly? It would be the worst purchase of anyone's life. But it would make a great doorstop.

script.action: Silence. Morgan closes their eyes. Kim starts to laugh.

script.say: Do you know how many shops I've been in today?
No.
Six. Every single salesperson told me this toaster was perfect. "Fast." "Amazing." "It changed my life."
Ha. Well. Other shops.
You're the first person who has told me the truth.

script.action: Kim takes out a small card and shows it to Morgan.

script.say: I work for the consumer protection office. We check shops that sell products with false claims. This toaster is on our list.
The consumer... protection...
Your shop has four hundred of them in the back, I believe?
Who told you that?
I did. Yesterday. On the phone. You asked how many we had.
So here's what happens. You can't sell these as smart, fast or life-changing any more. You can only sell them honestly.
Honestly? Nobody can sell this honestly!
Then you'd better buy one yourself. To show you believe in it.

script.action: Long pause. Morgan takes out a wallet, defeated. Vince steps behind the table, very professional.

script.say: Excellent choice, Morgan. That's three hundred, please.

script.action: Morgan hands over the money. Vince hands over the toaster.

script.say: Any last words?
Honestly? Worst money you'll ever spend.

script.action: Kim shakes Vince's hand. Morgan hugs the toaster sadly. Blackout.

ul: Put the counter centre stage with the toaster facing the audience. Vince stands beside it, Kim on the customer side, and Morgan at a pretend shelf a few steps away, always watching.
Morgan creeps closer each time Vince fails, until Morgan physically pushes in. The distance between them shows the pressure.
The toaster can be any box with stickers, a cardboard slot and a phone light inside. The sad beep is a phone sound or someone offstage.
When Kim shows the card, Kim should turn to Morgan, not Vince, so the audience sees the power move to the right person.
Land the ending as a mirror of the start: Vince is now the confident one behind the counter, Morgan is the customer, and the last line is said with real kindness.
The game is the fight between Vince's mouth and his brain. Before each truth, show a short physical struggle: jaw tight, hand on the throat, then the truth falls out.
Three escalations: features, then price, then the big question about the best purchase. Make the struggle longer and the truth bigger each time.
Vince is never mean about the toaster. He's sorry. The truth hurts him more than anyone.
Morgan's line through a smile is the funniest when nothing moves but the eyes.
Kim gives nothing away. Laugh only once, after the doorstop line. If Kim smiles too early, the twist is spoiled.
Common mistake: rushing the forty minutes of waiting. Let the silence after pressing the button go on longer than feels comfortable.
Change the product to anything terrible: a phone case that makes calls worse, a pillow that sings, a self-stirring spoon that only stirs anticlockwise.
Make it a school market: a student who cannot lie selling cupcakes that went badly wrong, with a teacher as the secret judge.
Part-two hook: Morgan wakes up the next day and also cannot lie, just in time for the shop's big sale.

prompts.keyframe: A nervous salesman with a name badge beside a strange decorated toaster on a shop counter, a curious customer facing him, a smiling manager watching from a shelf, bright shop lighting, wide shot, cinematic still, 16:9
shots: Medium close-up, static, a salesman struggles visibly to speak, jaw tight and hand at his throat, then gives up and speaks with an apologetic face, comedic mood
Two-shot, a salesman and customer stare at a toaster with a blinking light in total silence, slow push in, awkward comedic timing
Wide shot, a customer calmly shows a small ID card to a shocked shop manager while the salesman watches, then the manager sadly hugs the toaster

faq.q: Can we use The Honest Salesman for a drama class or upload it to a monetised channel?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0 for classes, performances, competitions and videos, including monetised ones. Credit "Script: cv.cm".

faq.q: How should Vince show that he physically cannot lie?
faq.a: Pick one clear physical habit and repeat it: the jaw locks, the hand goes to the throat, the eyes fight. Each time the struggle is a little longer, then the true words come out quickly, as if escaping.

faq.q: Can we turn this into a two-person scene?
faq.a: Yes. Cut Morgan and give the pressure to Kim, who keeps asking Vince to say something nice. Keep the inspector reveal, but Kim then asks Vince to help check other shops.
